trace.hy_filter_activation_rationale: All four relevance criteria are evidenced. Multiple organisational logics are explicit; structural asymmetry is relevant because institutional stakeholders, producers of evidence and public audiences possess different authority and exposure; translation is the constitutive mechanism connecting qualitative evidence to public and institutional use; and the process is required to materialize into traceable public-facing outputs and actionable recommendations.

evidence: The description explicitly refers to multiple organisational logics.
Research rigor, editorial accessibility, stakeholder responsiveness, operational delivery and trace governance impose different standards on the work.
Competing institutional expectations are explicitly named.
The role mediates between institutional expectations and public-facing communication, implying unequal authority over framing and approval.
Evidence producers, organisational stakeholders and public audiences have different capacities to determine how material is interpreted and used.
The role is assigned broad coordination responsibility while its own decision authority is not defined.
The role must translate complex qualitative material into clear public-facing outputs.
Stakeholder communication must connect competing institutional expectations to editorial and analytical work.
Translation changes evidence into forms that can be publicly understood and institutionally acted upon; it is not merely cosmetic rewriting.
Traceability, durable artifact persistence and result retrieval make materialized and reviewable products central to the test purpose.
